name: IDs that survive uninstall (Keychain, Block Store)
plain: iOS Keychain items and Android Block Store data can outlive an uninstall.
meaning: Lets an app re-recognize a returning person after delete and reinstall. Keychain items often remain after app deletion; Block Store also restores to a new phone.

android.persistence: Until device wipe or user clears
android.api_surface: Block Store API (Play services); Auto Backup
android.note: Block Store: up to 16 items of up to 4 KB each, end-to-end encrypted backup

ios.api_surface: Keychain items often remain after app deletion; iCloud Keychain can sync them

limits.headline: Can keep a small stored ID that may come back after you delete and reinstall
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app saves it quietly while you use it
can: Save a secret or ID in the iPhone Keychain that often stays after the app is deleted
Save up to 16 items of up to 4 KB each in Android Block Store
Sync saved items to a new device through iCloud Keychain or Google backup
Recognize you when you reinstall the app
cannot: Survive a full device wipe or reset
Be seen by apps from other developers
Keep growing on Android; Block Store caps the number and size of items
Come back on Android if you turn off backup or Google blocks the restore
limits.differs: iPhone Keychain items often stay by default. Android needs Block Store or Auto Backup, and you can turn backup off.

story.what_it_is: Small saved data that stays on your phone or in the cloud even after you delete the app.

marketing.name: Block Store
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: save credentials or small data so users can restore their sign in on a new Android device.

story.for_you: After you delete and reinstall an app, it may still know who you are and sign you in without a password. You might see that as helpful. You will not see that the app also remembers things you thought were wiped.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to restore sign in after a phone upgrade and to stop abuse, like free trials claimed over and over. The same trick also lets a company recognize a returning person after a clean install.

use_cases.example: You buy a new phone and the game signs you in and brings your saved profile back with no password.
A shopping app remembers a coupon was used on this phone even after you reinstall.
A wallet app notices a reinstall by the same person and avoids sending a second verification text.
A dating or banking app spots a banned user who deleted the app and started again.
A streaming app limits a free trial to one per phone, even if you remove and add the app.
An ad firm keeps a stable ID that outlives uninstall so campaign results are not broken by reinstalls.

story.android_note: Block Store can also move data to a new phone, and Auto Backup can restore app data.
story.ios_note: Keychain items often remain after the app is deleted, and the person cannot easily see or clear them.
